title: Bindings
description: Viewer bindings (spec: "Visualization and bindings"). Bindings are stored with the model and reference scene names and signal ids only, never solver internals.

binding.title: Binding
binding.description: One binding: a scene target, a property, the signal(s) that drive it, and optional gain and offset.

segmentBinding.title: SegmentBinding
segmentBinding.description: A bar between two moving points, such as a truss member between two pin nodes. Each frame the viewer places the visual (a box or a cylinder) so that its `axis` runs from end point A to end point B: the visual is centred between the points, turned onto the line A-B and stretched along `axis` to the distance |AB| (its cross-section keeps its size). The binding replaces the visual's pose in its link. `axis` is the visual-local direction that runs from A to B (default +z for a cylinder, its own axis, and +x for a box). `broken` is an optional failure flag of the bar (for example a Truss2D `failed[k]` or a Bar2D `broken`): above 0.5 the bar is drawn as `brokenStyle`. Colour the bar with a `color` binding of the same visual (for example a utilisation signal on the coolwarm colormap) and hide it with a `visible` binding.

signal.description: The end points, A then B, in metres in the world frame: 4 signals (uA, vA, uB, vB) for a planar model, mapped into the world by `plane` and `depth`, or 6 signals (xA, yA, zA, xB, yB, zB). The count is checked by the viewer (E304: 4 or 6).

depth.description: Planar end points only: the world coordinate along the third axis (y for the xz plane), in m. Default 0.

gain.description: Multiplies every end point coordinate (default 1), for example 0.001 for coordinates in mm.

offset.description: Added to every end point coordinate after the gain (default 0).

segmentPlane.title: SegmentPlane
segmentPlane.description: The world plane of planar end points (u, v): xy maps them to (u, v, depth), xz to (u, depth, v), yz to (depth, u, v). Default xz: a planar model with y up stands upright in the Z-up world.

segmentBrokenStyle.title: SegmentBrokenStyle
segmentBrokenStyle.description: How a broken bar is drawn: snapped (two stubs, about 40 % of the length each, hang from the end points with a gap between them) or hidden. Default snapped.

signal.description: Exactly 7 signals, in this fixed order: quaternion then position, (q_w, q_x, q_y, q_z, x, y, z), the same chart as the model's spatial pose Vec{7} (PoseIntegrator3D, ComposePose3D, JointTransform3D). The scalar quaternion part q_w comes first and the position is in metres in the world frame. The count is checked by the viewer (E304); the viewer must not reorder or infer the order from signal names.

deformationBinding.title: DeformationBinding
deformationBinding.description: Elastic deformation of a beam-shaped visual (a box or a cylinder) by modal coordinates (assumed modes, Euler-Bernoulli), or by the twist of a lumped torsion spring (basis linear). The beam frame has its origin at end A (s = 0) and its x axis along the beam to end B (s = L). "bending-y" deflects along the beam y axis (sections rotate about z by the slope), "bending-z" along the beam z axis (sections rotate about y), "torsion" rotates the sections about x. Deflection w(s) = sum_n phi_n(s) * eta_n (eta in m), twist theta(s) = sum_n psi_n(s) * eta_n (eta in rad), with the mode shapes of `basis` normalised to (1/L) * integral_0^L phi_n^2 ds = 1. Deformation bindings of one visual (at most one per family) compose and must give the same `beam`. The rigid motion of the beam frame is the pose binding of the link the visual belongs to.

signal.description: The modal coordinates eta_1..eta_n of the family, one signal per mode in mode order (1 to 3 modes). Bending coordinates are in m, torsion coordinates in rad. A FlexibleBeam block records them as <Block>/eta_y[i], <Block>/eta_z[i] and <Block>/eta_t[i].

gain.description: Multiplies every modal coordinate (default 1), e.g. 0.001 for coordinates in mm. The viewer's exaggeration factor is a display setting and is not stored in the binding.

deformationBasis.title: DeformationBasis
deformationBasis.description: Boundary conditions of the mode shapes. clamped-free: end A clamped to the beam frame, end B free (cantilever). free-free: both ends free (the rigid motion is the beam frame pose). linear: the lumped (massless spring) twist distribution of a torsion spring, theta(s) = (s / L) * eta, where the single coordinate eta is the twist of end B relative to end A in rad; torsion only, exactly one signal (a semantic rule, not a schema rule: the viewer reports a linear bending binding as E301 and a second signal as E304, like the run checks).

beamMapping.title: BeamMapping
beamMapping.description: Where the beam frame sits in the visual. `axis` is the visual-local direction from end A to end B; end A is the face of the shape on the other side (boxes and cylinders are centred on their origin, so end A is at -extent/2 along `axis`). `y` is the visual-local direction of the beam y axis, perpendicular to `axis` (default: +y, or +z when `axis` is along y); the beam z axis is axis x y. A cylinder's own axis is its local z, so a cylinder takes `axis` +z or -z.

length.description: Beam length L in m: the mode shapes run over s = 0..L from end A. Default: the extent of the shape along `axis`. Parts of the shape beyond L move rigidly with the section at L.

strainColor.title: StrainColor
strainColor.description: Colours the visual by the bending strain magnitude along the beam, c * |w''(s)|, with c the distance of the outer fibre from the neutral axis (half the box size across the beam, or the cylinder radius), over the bending families of the visual. Uses the true deformation, never the exaggerated one. `range` is in strain (dimensionless, e.g. [0, 0.001]).
